newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Surveillance says PSI factor may hurt '97.
newsitem.headline: Surveillance says PSI factor may hurt '97.

text.p: Swiss inspection and testing group Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) Holdings SA said on Monday that problems remain in Pakistan and Indonesian business which could have a negative impact on its 1997 earnings.
The problems pertain to preshipment inspection (PSI) contracts with the governments of Pakistan and Indonesia.
"As announced on January 13, 1997, the interim government of Pakistan has unexpectedly taken the decision to terminate the PSI programme with SGS, with effect from March 12, 1997," Surveillance said.
"In view of the situation, SGS has now suspended its PSI services and is continuing discussions with the new government," it said.
It also noted a previously announced termination by the Indonesian government of an existing PSI contract from March 31, 1997.
"SGS is presently discussing measures to assist the customs and the implementation of the new law, but is not in a position today to comment on the outcome of these discussions," Surveillance said.

"The combined effect of the termination of the PSI contract with Pakistan, together with a potential change in the relationship of SGS with the government of Indonesia, would have a negative impact on the group's 1997 profits," it said.
